title: Neon Alley Brawl
observed_goal: In the menu frame, the textual goal is «START BRAWL»; the official card describes the goal as progressing through an alley, fighting enemies, and reaching the boss, but reaching this goal was not observed in the frames.
observed_controls: The guide screen announces movement with WASD or L-Stick; acceptance of this input was not confirmed in the recorded run.

The guide screen announces light attack with J/LMB, heavy attack/guard break with K/RMB, jump with Space, roll with L/Shift, grab/pick up/drop with I/E, and pause with Esc; successful execution of none of these was directly observed.
The input metadata records Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight+Space; visual change alone does not establish their acceptance.
observed_core_loop: Direct evidence of active gameplay was seen: the HUD, timer, and level scene are present in the after_key_burst, after_combined_input, and late frames, and the time advances from 0:01 to 0:03 and 0:05. The complete movement/combat/progression/outcome cycle or a clear repetition was not observed.
progress_feedback: In the gameplay frames, the timer, zero score, status bar, and x3 counter are visible; score increase, bar change, hit count, or level progression was not observed. The page text also showed only 81% download progress during loading.
decisions_risk_reward: The guide text claims the existence of choices involving light/heavy attack, jumping, rolling, and using environmental objects, but no decision, risk, reward, or successful interaction was directly seen in the execution frames.
rewards: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; the official card claims chaining combos and fighting to the boss, but no reward or executed combo was recorded in the frames.
penalties_failure: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no loss, damage, health reduction, or direct penalty is visible in the frames.
outcomes_replay: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no win/loss result, level ending, replay screen, or repeating cycle was recorded.
onboarding: The load frame shows a start menu with the START BRAWL button and a CONTROLS option. The after_start frame displays a control guide screen and the Enter LET'S GO button. This is screen-based instruction and does not establish successful execution of the commands.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a pixel-art visual style, high-contrast neon, and a readable HUD. EN/中文 language selection is visible in the menu. Reliable information about audio, subtitles, accessibility settings, or audio feedback was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The metadata records a canvas with dimensions 1280×800 and a loaded image with a natural size of 1280×720; this is only a technical clue and does not establish game behavior.
The technical log reports Godot Engine v4.7.2, Emscripten 4.0.20, WebGL 2.0, and single-threaded execution; these are possible technical clues, not evidence of design or accepted input.
Three WebGL software fallback warnings and one HTTP 403 error are recorded in the console; their effect on the game experience is not determinable from this evidence.
The script scan reports 0 scripts and 0 bytes, and no engine marker or tuning constant candidate was recorded; this result is limited to the available capture.
transferable_principles: Provide instruction before entering the game in a short, readable screen and connect inputs to visible action.
Progress feedback should be visible within the scene through stable, interpretable indicators.
For high-risk actions, make the difference between a safe state and danger clear through direct, visible feedback.
Maintain a clear boundary between what the introduction card claims and what was tested in the actual run.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, every score/rank should reflect only gameplay skill and performance; this evidence provides no basis for connecting it to a purchase or wallet, and the advantage should not come from a purchase/wallet.
A short tutorial and stable progress indicators may serve as inspiration, but only after direct testing of the Candle Climber gameplay loop.

Do not make free brake, horizontal direction change, or a branching path requiring new controls a definite recommendation; each is only a hypothesis requiring testing and was not tested in this analysis.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce or propose this game's names, characters, art, level, text, sounds, brands, or assets.
Do not treat the claimed combo, environmental weapon, enemy, or reaching the boss as a confirmed feature of the execution.
Do not consider change between frames alone to be evidence of input acceptance or successful mechanics.
Do not take the absence of an enemy, outcome, or other element in the opening frame as evidence that it is absent from the entire game.

evidence.claim: The opening menu with the START BRAWL button, CONTROLS option, and «NO RECORD YET» indicator is visible.
The guide screen announces movement, attack, jump, roll, grab/pick up/drop, and pause controls and several mechanical tips; their execution was not observed in this frame.
The active HUD, 0:01 timer, 0000000 score, status bar, and level 1 title are visible in the frame.
The execution frame shows the 0:03 timer and an active character/scene; acceptance of the combined input or its mechanical effect has not been established.
In the late frame, the 0:05 timer and active scene are visible, but the score remains zero and the level outcome is not visible.
The official game card claims combo chaining, use of street objects as weapons, and progression to the boss; this claim was not tested through complete execution in the frames.
The metadata records visual change after interaction, but explicitly warns that the change may be caused by animation or passage of time and does not establish input comprehension.
The technical log reports Godot Engine v4.7.2, Emscripten 4.0.20, WebGL 2.0, and single-threaded execution.

limitations: The analysis uses only evidence.json and five frames from this game; no web browsing or replay was performed. The frames show the sequence from the menu to active gameplay, but no enemy, collision, combo, object use, progression, win/loss, or definite acceptance of any input was recorded in them. stage_text is empty after load, and changes between frames may be solely due to time or animation.
